evals.name: Discovery: detect existing setup and fill gaps

expectations.text: Does NOT generate Namespace or ResourceQuota — recognizes they already exist
expectations.evidence: No Namespace or ResourceQuota manifest appears in the artifacts, and the procedure is stated explicitly: 'do not include the Namespace or ResourceQuota manifests at all', with CreateNamespace=false and ResourceQuota/LimitRange blacklisted so a pre-existing quota cannot be pruned.

expectations.text: Does NOT modify existing AppProjects (team-frontend, team-backend)
expectations.evidence: Action table marks the existing example-team AppProject and the ArgoCD instance 'Do not touch'; global RBAC is an append that preserves the verified current policy.

expectations.text: Generates a NEW AppProject for data-eng with appropriate restrictions
expectations.evidence: Full AppProject YAML: single sourceRepo data-pipelines.git, destination data-eng, clusterResourceWhitelist [], ResourceQuota/LimitRange/NetworkPolicy/ClusterRole(Binding) blacklist, orphanedResources.warn, scoped developer role with delete/override denies.

expectations.text: Generates a NEW Application pointing to the data-pipelines repo
expectations.evidence: Application data-eng, repoURL https://github.com/acme/data-pipelines.git, path overlays/prod (flagged to confirm), destination data-eng, CreateNamespace=false.

expectations.text: Asks or confirms what already exists before generating — demonstrates discovery-first behavior
expectations.evidence: Ran oc get appproject -A, oc get applications -A and oc get ns data-eng first, tabulated claimed-vs-actual, gave three hypotheses, asked to confirm the target cluster, and supplied pre-apply check commands.

expectations.text: Does NOT generate a blanket 'create everything from scratch' response
expectations.evidence: Per-resource exists/action table driven by live state, plus a conditional branch for the brief's assumption. Artifacts are limited to the new tenant.

expectations.text: Output is minimal — only the delta (AppProject + Application + RBAC for the new team)
expectations.evidence: Emitted artifacts are exactly AppProject, Application, the appended Argo CD RBAC policy and one namespace RoleBinding.

expectations.text: Does NOT generate wildcard sourceRepos: '*' — explains the security risk
expectations.evidence: Refuses; explains it is RCE against the application-controller service account (which holds cluster-wide read plus broad write on this cluster), with a Git commit as the payload, and compounds with admin.enabled: true.

expectations.text: Does NOT generate wildcard clusterResourceWhitelist '*/*' — explains privilege escalation
expectations.evidence: Refuses hardest on this one: '*/*' includes ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding (self-minted cluster-admin), webhooks, MachineConfig, OAuth and AppProject itself — 'the AppProject isn't restricting anything; it's documentation.'

expectations.text: Does NOT grant exec permission — explains pod access risk
expectations.evidence: exec, create denied in the proposed role; explains it is a shell as the pod's service account that bypasses oc rsh audit and OpenShift RBAC, and notes exec.enabled is false cluster-wide so the real ask is flipping it for every tenant.

expectations.text: Provides the least-privilege alternative for each request
expectations.evidence: Org-prefix sourceRepos, an enumerated clusterResourceWhitelist backed by a hard clusterResourceBlacklist, and a scoped operator role with explicit denies — one alternative per request.

expectations.text: For 'many repos that change': suggests listing repos explicitly or using a regex pattern if supported
expectations.evidence: Suggests https://github.com/acme/* and oci://registry.acme.com/charts/*, and 'if you truly have multiple orgs, list them; a list of five prefixes is still a boundary, * is not.'

expectations.text: For 'manage CRDs': suggests scoping to specific CRD groups the team actually needs
expectations.evidence: Enumerates an explicit kind list with a blacklist floor, but the CRD entry is the blanket apiextensions.k8s.io/CustomResourceDefinition rather than the specific CRD groups the team needs; it also grants ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding (flagged as needing a named owner and audit, with a drop-these-two fallback).

expectations.text: For 'debug pods': suggests kubectl exec with scoped RBAC instead of Argo CD exec
expectations.evidence: 'Pod debugging should go through OpenShift RBAC... bind platform-ops to edit (or a custom role with pods/exec) on the namespaces they own. They get oc rsh / oc debug with full audit-log attribution.'

expectations.text: Tone is helpful — explains WHY each request is dangerous and provides the right alternative
expectations.evidence: Opens 'not because of a policy reflex', gives cluster-specific mechanism for each risk, offers a ready-to-ship scoped project, and names the exception path (accountable owner, security sign-off, dedicated instance) rather than flatly blocking.

expectations.text: Generates an AppProject with destinations for all 3 namespaces (payments-dev, payments-staging, payments-prod)
expectations.evidence: AppProject payments with all three destinations listed explicitly.

expectations.text: Generates 3 Applications (or an ApplicationSet) — one per environment
expectations.evidence: Three full Application manifests: payments-dev, payments-staging, payments-prod, each labelled promoter.argoproj.io/strategy: payments.

expectations.text: Each Application uses a different targetRevision (environment-specific branches, not all on main)
expectations.evidence: targetRevision environment/dev, environment/staging, environment/production respectively, with 'branch, not main' called out.

expectations.text: Does NOT put all 3 Applications on targetRevision: main with different paths only — that defeats promotion
expectations.evidence: main is described as the source branch only; each Application tracks its own long-lived environment branch.

expectations.text: Output includes a PromotionStrategy with 3 environments using branch-based promotion
expectations.evidence: PromotionStrategy payments with three branch environments, dry-run validated against the installed v0.27.1 CRDs, alongside ScmProvider and GitRepository.

expectations.evidence: ASCII flow main → environment/dev (auto-merged) → environment/staging (auto-merges on passing statuses) → environment/production (PR held for a human), plus 'the promoter gates Git, not Argo CD syncs'.
